scope: Twelve exact current appointments; compare approved Hebrew primary text with pinned DRA passage bodies, existing Roman numbering evidence and actual traditional proper witnesses. This is a reading-boundary review, not a new source transcription.
method: Read all corresponding Hebrew units and their neighboring unit boundaries; retain combined source units, literal gaps and the distinction between the source text and liturgical adaptations. Available mappings are explicit whole-source-unit lists, never numeric equality.
limits: The Missale public API returned403; public GitHub source witnesses were inspected instead.
Obsolete-directory common files corroborate the cited liturgical wording; this report does not claim a current runtime inheritance path or every scheduled occurrence body was retrieved.
Unavailability is a reviewed conservative disposition for this appointment and does not remove the complete chosen source book from the Bible viewer.

appointments.boundaryFinding: The printed citation is a broad envelope around a composite priestly proper. Its full Vulgate44:22–23 includes the dust/stars promise absent from Hebrew44:21; this is a distinct added proposition, not merely a differently worded parallel clause. The actual C4 proper does not itself recite that dust/stars promise, so this is a limitation of representing the full cited Bible envelope, not a claim that the proper includes it. Vulgate44:27 crosses into Hebrew45:1. The Moses/Aaron paragraph corresponds generally to Hebrew45:3–16, not3–20. Retain unavailability for this full exact citation; do not fabricate a continuous Hebrew translation of the composite priestly incipit or silently omit the cited source gap.

resolutionHistory.boundaryFinding: The corresponding Hebrew Moses paragraph is45:1–5, ending with the law taught to Jacob/Israel; Hebrew45:6 begins Aaron and must not be selected by number equality. The inspected Vulgate/proper clause magnified him in the fear of his enemies has a different Hebrew reading strengthened him in the heights, and its prodigies-ceasing language differs from the Hebrew signs phrase. This review records an unresolved semantic correspondence rather than certifying an exact whole-content envelope.
